definition: A model design where an encoder processes an input sequence into a representation, and a decoder generates an output sequence from that representation.
details: This architecture underlies many sequence-to-sequence tasks like machine translation and summarization; the original transformer paper used this design, though many modern LLMs use decoder-only variants instead.
story: Think of a jazz musician who has heard so many solos that a new one simply falls out of their fingers. Boil it down and it is this: A model design where an encoder processes an input sequence into a representation, and a decoder generates an output sequence from that representation. Here is why it matters: This architecture underlies many sequence-to-sequence tasks like machine translation and summarization; the original transformer paper used this design, though many modern LLMs use decoder-only variants instead. Creation, here, is memory recombined at speed. That next-word, next-stroke magic is Encoder-Decoder Architecture.
